text: Imagine waking up to find insects as big as people.
Ants, beetles and bees, as big as us.
Some are now a hundred times their normal size.
Insects have no lungs, just tiny breathing holes.
Air creeps in through thin tubes.
At this size, oxygen can't reach the middle.
Within an hour, many collapse.
Weight grows much faster than strength.
Heavy armour makes thin legs buckle.
The bee's wings are now far too small.
Only cockroaches and beetles keep crawling.
The survivors are starving, and they eat everything.
Gardens and fields are stripped bare.
Roads jam, cars are abandoned, and people flee.
A month later, the last ants survive the only way they can: together.
Their nest is a city of tunnels.
Air shafts carry fresh air to the queen.
But giant insects were real.
Dragonflies once grew 70 centimetres wide.
The air then held 35% oxygen.
Today there's only 21%.
Luckily, the air we breathe keeps insects small.
